title: The Sensory-Motor Stage (Piaget): How Your Child Learns About the World Through the Senses and Movement
summary: In the first year, the child is in the 'sensory-motor stage' (Piaget)—learning about the world through the five senses and movement (grasping, rolling, crawling, walking). The brain builds mental maps for every sensory experience. Early hyperactivity is not a 'problem' but a driver of exploration—the child runs, jumps, and throws to test gravity, space, cause, and effect. Your role: provide a safe environment for free movement (a mat, cushions, crawling space), and minimize time spent sitting in seats/strollers. Movement = learning.
try_this: This week: observe your child for 10 minutes while they play freely—do not direct or correct. Note: what movements do they repeat? What materials attract them? Do they use both hands together? These observations are your guide to what their brain is developing now.
reflection_prompts: Do you feel anxious when your child moves a lot? How do you handle this feeling?
What space is available for your child’s free movement in your home? Can it be increased?
